# USB Gym plug-slot leaderboard

<!-- generated by `python -m usbg.leaderboard render`; do not edit by hand -->

Every row runs the plug protocol: one slot swapped at a time, the rest of the loop at that slot's condition, the same 60 held-out episodes (six held-out patients, evaluation seed 999, contact on) at 12 steps. Error: final translation error in mm, mean over seeds of patient means (lower is better). Difference: from the slot's reference component, paired by seed, with its 95% paired t CI and the patients of 6 sharing its sign. Seeds: the seeds, of 3, whose own difference shares that sign (n/a for a seed-0 row). Holm p: within the slot's pre-specified family. TOST: yes when the 90% paired t CI lies inside ±1 mm (post hoc, unadjusted). Decision: the pre-specified outcome words; a decision of no detectable difference is not powered for equivalence.

Order (as in Table C.1, Appendix C of the article): in each slot the reference comes first, then the rows whose difference is taken from it, by mean error (unrounded), lowest first, with the privileged rows last. Rows run at seed 0 only follow the reference's seed-0 line in the same order, indented, since their differences are taken from that line and their error is that of one seed. The CT-anatomy rows keep the order of Table 5, since each is scored against its own reference level. Rows submitted after the article come after the published rows of their slot, in a group of their own that is outside this order and not indented, whatever their seeds. The pretrained-backbone differences, which have no error of their own, are listed under the mask-source table, outside the order.

Role: the row's group in Table 5 (reference, family, second family, secondary or privileged); second family: the second mask-source family or the LPIPS reward family; privileged: the group of privileged rows, which are secondary; submitted: a row added after the article.

The order is by mean error only and is not a ranking. Each row was tested against its slot's reference, not against the other rows, and where the decision is no detectable difference, the methods are not distinguished from the reference or from each other. At n = 6 held-out patients, a result is an estimate with its interval, read beside coverage and cost.

Rows from Table 5 of the USB Gym article are listed as published and are recomputed from their per-episode values by `python -m usbg.leaderboard recompute` (and by the tests). Rows added after the article are marked **submitted**: they are post hoc and outside the pre-specified families, so their p is the unadjusted paired t p, no Holm adjustment applies and they get no pre-specified decision word; a row with three seeds also shows its patient-by-seed bootstrap interval (Appendix B of the article). To add a method, see [SUBMITTING.md](SUBMITTING.md).

Marks: ᴸ reads the CT label slice; † privileged (simulator state that no rig provides); ‡ fewer seeds than designed; ᵃ unadjusted CI excludes 0, not declared a difference after Holm (post hoc note); ᵉ equivalence within ±1 mm not shown. Every contrast is conditional on the trained artifacts; seeds index artifacts and the patient is the sampling unit. All results are in simulation.

## CT anatomy

Condition: five reference levels of the oracle ladder, each in its oracle-ladder condition with seeds 0 to 2. TotalSegmentator v2 labels (fast mode, 3.0 mm) replace the reference labels on the same episodes and classes. Each row is that level minus the same level on the reference labels. Families: CT-anatomy difference (paired t, Holm, m = 5) and CT-anatomy equivalence (TOST with a ±1 mm margin, Holm over the TOST p values, m = 5); the Decision column carries both families' outcomes, and the TOST column is the unadjusted TOST of every row. The trained artifacts never saw the new labels, so a change mixes label noise with the shift between training and evaluation labels. All 19 CTs are in TotalSegmentator's own training data, so these labels are in-sample predictions: the rows are a label-noise sensitivity check, not a test of an independent CT segmenter.

## Combination and benchmark baseline

The combination is defined as the authors' original pipeline with the SSIM appearance term in the REINFORCE reward, the only slot the pre-specified combination rule changed; chosen per slot on the 6 held-out patients and tested on 20 CTs of the replication cohort. It is a whole pipeline, not a slot row, so it has no row in the slot tables above. Final translation error (mm); the six held-out patients took part in the choice, so their values are selection-biased and for estimation only. On the cohort CTs the static start ends at 15.97 mm and the pose oracle (privileged) at 1.47 mm.

The benchmark baseline is, separately with physics and with SonoSPADE frames, the better of two pipelines on the 20 cohort CTs: the authors' original pipeline or, where it tests lower, the combination. With physics frames it is the authors' original pipeline, 15.36 mm (D-P: the combination holds higher); with SonoSPADE frames it is the combination, 13.70 mm (D-S: it holds lower).

| Frames | Patients | Combination | Authors' original pipeline | The combination's learned-mask servo base |

| physics | 6 held-out patients | 16.62 | 16.73 | 17.20 |
| SonoSPADE | 20 cohort CTs | 13.70 | 13.96 | 13.71 |
| SonoSPADE | 6 held-out patients | 13.10 | 13.11 | 13.13 |
